correctness.rationale: For uniformly small changes, the area of a polygon with fixed normal fan is exactly quadratic in support offsets. The covariogram \(g_P(tu)=|P\cap(P+tu)|\) is obtained from inward offsets \(t\max(0,-n_i\cdot u)\). Three elementary cosine integrals give \(C_4(P)=\sum_i[1+(\pi-\alpha_i)\cot\alpha_i]/(8\pi^2)\), including perimeter normalization. Differentiation of \(H(\beta)=(\sin\beta-\beta\cos\beta)/\sin^3\beta\) gives \(f^{\prime\prime}(a)>2/3\); the constrained Jensen argument yields the exact factor \(1/(24\pi^2)\). The centrally symmetric even-sided equilateral polygon has squared-angle variance \(4\varepsilon^2\) and approaches the same quotient as the number of sides tends to infinity, proving optimality. The packaged standard-library program independently checks finite polygon clipping and angular integrals, but is not a substitute for the analytic proof.

originality.rationale: The accepted statement is the universal sharp angle-rigidity inequality for the short-pair quartic coefficient, together with its exact angle formula and all-side-count sharpness. Wang 2026 establishes only the perimeter small-distance correction. Pure–Durrani–Tong–Pan 2019 and Tong–Pan 2016 present general algorithms for distance distributions but do not state the angle-only sharp minimization or dimension-free variance stability; their methods may implicitly generate the coefficient and are explicitly credited. Full public mathematical stability reports concern reduced-polygon area and tangential-quadrilateral semiperimeter, not this statistic. Specific older broad polygon-distance literature has incomplete full-text access, and undocumented equivalences remain a residual risk.

value.rationale: This is a motivated exact natural short-pair statistic newly foregrounded by Wang 2026; the fourth-order coefficient isolates polygon angular geometry beyond area/perimeter. For every allowed vertex count, it solves a complete natural minimization, characterizes equality, and gives a quantitative stability inequality with the best possible coefficient uniform across all side counts. The all-N optimality construction and angle-only covariance calculation are substantive geometry, not arbitrary parameter slicing or a mere existing table recomputation.
